Users in Europe complained about latency.

We copied the US stack to eu-west-1, pointed DNS at both, and called it multi-region.

A week later: duplicate order IDs, conflicting profile updates, wrong cart states.

We built active-active without designing for conflicts. 🧵

Multi-region is not one architecture:

• Latency → reads near users
• Availability → survive region loss
• Compliance → data stays in-region

"Deploy twice" is easy. Writes across regions are the hard part.

Active-passive: one write primary, DR region on standby.
✅ Simpler consistency
❌ Idle cost, failover RPO/RTO

Active-active: regions serve writes concurrently.
✅ Local latency + no idle region
❌ Conflicts, routing, ops complexity

Stepping stone most teams need first:

Read local (replica + CDN)
Write global primary OR partition by region

Not: two regions both mutating the same row with no conflict strategy.

If you can't name your conflict resolution (LWW, home region, CRDT, version check), you don't have active-active — you have a latent bug.

Failover needs RTO/RPO targets + split-brain guards. Rehearse it.
